confidence_note: The 'Unexpected' chapter of Made to Stick includes the story of Nora Ephron's high school journalism teacher, who asked students to write the lead for a story about the faculty going to a conference; after students summarized the facts, he revealed the lead: 'There will be no school next Thursday.' The chapter also discusses surprise as a way to get attention and George Loewenstein's 'gap theory' of curiosity: curiosity arises when we feel a gap in our knowledge, and good communicators open such gaps and then fill them. Details are paraphrased; Ephron's recollection is well documented in the book.
facts: Nora Ephron, later a famous screenwriter, remembered her first day of high school journalism class.
The teacher gave students a set of facts: the school's faculty would travel to a conference the next Thursday, with names of speakers including notable figures.
The students wrote leads that summarized the facts in order: who, what, where, when.
The teacher read them, then revealed the lead he wanted: 'There will be no school next Thursday.'
Ephron said it was a revelation: journalism was about figuring out the point, not repeating the facts.

The Heaths use surprise to show how to get attention, and describe George Loewenstein's 'gap theory' of curiosity: curiosity happens when we feel a gap in our knowledge, and it creates an itch we want to scratch.
To hold attention, they suggest opening knowledge gaps first, and then closing them.
tension: A class of students gets every fact right and still misses the story completely.
opening_idea: A teacher reads his students' carefully written news leads, then shows them the one sentence they all missed.

lessons.idea: Find the point, not just the facts.

lessons.idea: Open a curiosity gap to hold attention.
